authority.topological_order_source: scripts/lib/solver.mjs :: solveCase(...).solve_order_evidence (P4.7 Tarjan at solve time)
authority.note: Locality is asserted against the equation graph's OWN active edge set for the case's declared circularity. No second dependency relation is invented here: a change is lawful only where the canonical graph already says a path exists.

observation_planes.observable: every forecast-period field classified economic below, rounded to 9 decimal places, plus converged and all_checks_pass
observation_planes.primitive_note: The canary hashes 23 forecast fields; the phase-9 twin hashes emitted J/K/L cells of one sheet. This plane's signature covers all 72 economic forecast fields plus instrument_results and statement_values, so it is a strict superset of the canary's key set. The suite proves the superset containment rather than asserting it.

observation_planes.observable: the first line of the thrown message, split into its literal text and its embedded numeric magnitudes
observation_planes.primitive_note: A case the pipeline lawfully refuses has no economics to preserve, but its REFUSAL must still be label-independent. This plane carries the economics-preserving families over the refused population.

comparison.literal_text: compared EXACTLY — a different reason, a different case id or a different word is a violation
comparison.numeric_magnitudes: compared EXACTLY — a printed magnitude that moves at all is a violation
comparison.why_exact: This comparison WAS made at a declared relative epsilon of 1e-9, on the stated ground that a reported residual is a floating-point sum whose ORDER the instrument register determines. P7.10 closed that order dependence by construction (scripts/lib/canonical_sum.mjs sums a multiset in an order derived only from the values), so the justification no longer exists and the epsilon was removed rather than left standing behind a repaired defect. P7.9 verified the removal was safe before making it: across the whole refusal plane — 1,658 comparisons, 8 economics-preserving families over 208 refused cases — there is not one comparison that passes only because of the epsilon and not one non-zero drift, so exact comparison is strictly stronger and costs nothing. The mode is declared here rather than as a constant in the comparator so that re-loosening it is a visible change to this register; an undeclared mode throws.

forecast_field_class_semantics.graph_node_observable: The field is the forecast-plane realisation of exactly one equation-graph node. LOCALITY IS ASSERTED over this class: for an economics-changing transform, only the nodes forward-reachable from the perturbed node in the graph's own active edge set may move.
forecast_field_class_semantics.outside_equation_graph_coverage: A real economic quantity that NO equation-graph node stands for. P4.6 declares this gap (economic_coverage.uncovered_node_families: instrument, lease, acquisition, cash_bucket, statement_row, schedule_row, period). Economics-PRESERVING relations are asserted over this class at full strength; locality is NOT, because the graph carries no node to reach.
forecast_field_class_semantics.solver_diagnostic: Convergence bookkeeping, typed-state records and traces. Not an economic quantity: excluded from every signature and from locality, and named here so no field can be dropped silently.
forecast_field_class_semantics.identity: The period label. Carried in the signature as identity, never as an economic quantity.

cash.cash_interest_paid.unobservable_reason: The cash-flow interest bridge is not exposed as a forecast-record field; it is realised only in the emitted workbook row.

cash.net_finance_addback.unobservable_reason: Addback bridge row; the forecast record exposes the interest aggregates it is built from, not the addback.

cash.noncash_interest_addback.unobservable_reason: Addback bridge row; the forecast record exposes non_cash_interest, which is interest.noncash, not the addback.

control.circularity.unobservable_reason: The solver control carries no economic quantity by construction (P4.6 disposition solver_control).

debt.maturity_repayment.unobservable_reason: Per-instrument movement; the forecast record carries it only inside instrument_results, which P4.6 declares an uncovered instrument-family realisation.

debt.pik_accretion.unobservable_reason: Per-instrument principal accretion; realised in instrument_results (declared instrument-family gap).

debt.scheduled_amortisation.unobservable_reason: Per-instrument movement; realised in instrument_results (declared instrument-family gap).

interest.cash_income.unobservable_reason: Aggregated into interest.income before the forecast record; interest_income is the aggregate, so a separate observation would double-count the same field.

statement.finance_expense.unobservable_reason: The income-statement finance expense is not a forecast-record field; the record exposes the interest-schedule aggregate gross_interest, which is interest.gross_expense.

statement.finance_income.unobservable_reason: As statement.finance_expense — the record exposes interest_income, which is interest.income.

statement.cash_flow_start.unobservable_reason: The cash-flow anchor line is a workbook row; the forecast record exposes cash_from_operations, which is cash.cfo.

statement.effective_tax_rate.unobservable_reason: A ratio input. The forecast record carries tax and pre_tax_income, never the rate, so observing it would re-derive a quotient rather than read a value.

transform_families.rationale: A row's economic identity is carried by semantic_role and row_id; label is display text. If a synonym moves the economics, a label is being read as meaning.
The legal-form suffix (Limited / plc / Inc.) is part of the issuer's presented name. No economic quantity is a function of it.
A market suffix (.L, .O, ' US') distinguishes listing venues of one issuer. Venue is not an economic input.
Statement rows are addressed by row_id and semantic_role, never by array position. Reversing each section must not move a number.
transform_families.applicability_note: Most archetype cases declare one row per statement section, so reversing rows alone applies to 8. The family therefore reverses the ROW order within each section AND the SECTION traversal order, both of which are non-semantic, which lifts archetype applicability to every case with two or more sections.

transform_families.rationale: Instrument aggregates are sums over the register; each instrument keeps its own display_order, so presentation is untouched and the economics must be order-independent. This is also a floating-point-associativity probe.
transform_families.applicability_note: Only 2 of the 62 archetype cases carry two or more instruments, and the generated cohort cannot supply a multi-instrument SOLVABLE case: the generator pads an archetype's register with synthetic instruments, which the archetype's own debt_reconciliation opening-debt bridge then refuses (OPENING_DEBT_UNRESOLVED) or whose padded class the debt-class register refuses (lease_liability). Fabricating a matching reconciliation would be inventing evidence, so this family takes its volume from the REFUSAL plane, where ~200 multi-instrument generated cases live and where reordering the register must not change the refusal. The solve-plane floor is therefore 1.

transform_families.rationale: Leading, trailing, doubled and tab whitespace is an extraction artefact of the source document. It must not reach a number.
A column header repeated mid-table is the commonest paginated-PDF artefact. A row_type header carries no values, so two of them must be as economically inert as none.

declared_signature_exception.note: Applying this family exposed a real defect (MG-4): the inserted row_type header rows, which declare NO values at all, are materialised into the period's statement_values map as numeric 0. No solved economic quantity moves, so the family remains economics-preserving; the delta is PINNED to exactly this shape — only statement_values, only keys with this prefix, only the value 0, no key removed, no other field changed — rather than the relation being weakened.

transform_families.rationale: The unit phrase inside a label ($m, USDm, 'in millions') restates the SAME declared unit in different words. issuer.units is the sole unit authority; a unit phrase in display text must not be read as a second one.

targets: every declared monetary path of the case
transform_families.rationale: Restating the SAME economics from millions into thousands is the one unit transform that is not a relabel: the declared unit changes and every monetary magnitude changes with it. It is economics-changing with an EXACT expected change, which is what makes it a proof rather than a hash comparison.

expected_effect.currency_class_expectation: every currency-tolerance-class observable scales by exactly 1000
expected_effect.ratio_class_expectation: every ratio observable (net_leverage, and the ratio-tolerance-class node statement.effective_tax_rate) is INVARIANT

non_monetary_paths_held_fixed: rcf_policy.commitment_fee_value when commitment_fee_convention is a rate — the dimension is READ from unit_restatement_dimensions.discriminated_quantities, never inferred from the convention's spelling (D33)
statement rows whose semantic_role is effective_tax_rate
debt_reconciliation keys matching percentage / _rate / ratio / tolerance_bps

transform_families.rationale: The tightest locality claim the graph makes: statement.effective_tax_rate has exactly one outgoing edge, to statement.tax_expense, which reaches only statement.net_income. Two observables may move and twenty-four may not.

The minimum-cash floor enters the graph as a liquidity_constraint edge into rcf.draw and rcf.repayment, and with circularity on it reaches the whole interest-cash fixed point. The nodes it must NOT reach are EBIT, the tax rate, the debt schedule, the lease and every per-instrument interest node.
Lease principal repayment aggregates into debt.mandatory_repayment and from there into the cash waterfall. EBIT and the tax rate must not move.
Scheduled amortisation aggregates into debt.mandatory_repayment. EBIT and the tax rate must not move.
Debt issuance enters the cash waterfall directly. EBIT and the tax rate must not move.

generated_case_subspace.why_restricted: An economics-preserving relation over the economic_solve plane needs a case that HAS economics. The full P7.3 space is deliberately weighted into space the pipeline must refuse (one historical period, 52/53-week calendars, non-numeric opening balances, absent FX authority), where the only observable is the refusal. Those cases are NOT discarded: they carry the same economics-preserving families on the refusal_verdict plane.
generated_case_subspace.free_axes_note: Eleven axes are left free — accounting_framework, entity_type, filing_language_format, statement_topology, cash_flow_method, debt_instruments, broker_availability, acquisition_overlay, restructuring_complexity, identity_verdict, declared_language_adapter, refusal_pressure — so the sub-space still explores the declared dimension space rather than one point of it.

completion.why: generateCase carries six keys from its archetype seed shape (statement_structure, modules, controls, operating_metrics, forecast_assumptions, presentation_profile) and mints the rest, so the emitted model_case has no source_coverage, provenance or policy blocks and cannot enter the solver at all. The harness completes the case from the SAME seed shape it was generated against, and carries the archetype's execution_profile, so nothing is invented.
completion.carried_from_seed_shape: every top-level key the generator did not mint

known_defects.title: The canonical equation graph omits the cash-tax edge statement.tax_expense -> cash.cfo
known_defects.reproduction: Append an income-statement row {semantic_role: effective_tax_rate, values: [0.25,0.25,0.25,0.28,0.28,0.28]} and solve. tax moves 0 -> 42.27117623444384 and cash_from_operations moves 282.18090452260935 -> 239.69731031714127, so the operating cash flow depends on the tax charge. The graph gives statement.tax_expense exactly one outgoing edge, to statement.net_income, and anchors the cash flow at statement.ebit, so no path exists.
known_defects.second_order_consequence: The missing edge closes a cycle the repository does not declare: tax -> cfo -> ending_cash -> interest.cash_income -> interest.income -> statement.finance_income -> statement.pre_tax_income -> statement.tax_expense. assets/convergence-contract.v1.json declares ONE active SCC of 13 nodes for circularity 1 and it contains neither statement.pre_tax_income nor statement.tax_expense, yet both move under this perturbation. The declared fixed point therefore understates the solver's real fixed point.
known_defects.repair_owner: assets/equation-graph.v1.json + assets/convergence-contract.v1.json — both FORBIDDEN to this package. Recorded, not repaired.
known_defects.retirement_condition: When the edge lands, this suite fails at the reproduction assertion and this entry must be deleted.

known_defects.title: The equation graph has no debt or lease BALANCE node, so every balance movement -> accrued interest dependency is absent
known_defects.declared_elsewhere: scripts/lib/layered_graph_constitution.mjs :: EQUATION_GRAPH_UNCOVERED_NODE_FAMILIES declares the instrument and lease families uncovered (P4.6). That declaration is about ROW realisation; this entry states the same gap as concrete missing EDGES, which is what a locality relation needs.
known_defects.reproduction: Add 5 to every lease_policy.principal_repayment entry and solve: lease_interest moves, although the graph gives lease.principal one outgoing edge, to debt.mandatory_repayment. Symmetrically, adding 1 to instruments[0].scheduled_amortisation or 10 to instruments[0].new_issuance moves instrument_interest and non_cash_instrument_interest.
known_defects.repair_owner: assets/equation-graph.v1.json — FORBIDDEN to this package. Recorded, not repaired.
known_defects.retirement_condition: When a balance node or these edges land, this suite fails at the reproduction assertion and this entry must be updated or deleted.

known_defects.title: Solver convergence stops being scale-free above the declared reference magnitude, where a declared absolute ceiling binds instead — CORRECTED: the registered reproduction was D33's 350% commitment fee, not the tolerance
known_defects.reproduction: CORRECTED by P4.9 and P7.9. AS REGISTERED this entry claimed the transform's refusal proved a scale-dependent tolerance. It did not. D33 — a guard that tested the commitment-fee CONVENTION'S NAME against /rate/i, which no convention this repository admits matches — let unit_scale_restatement scale a 35bp fee to 35,000bp. The registered case then genuinely oscillates under a 350% commitment fee (residual pinned at ~7.07e4 through all 200 sweeps) and is CORRECTLY refused. The one generated reproduction, seed 700413, is the same shape. Held at a faithful rate the thousands restatement CONVERGES (residual 3.019e-9 against 1e-8, cash_from_operations exactly 1000x), and a faithful sweep at x1e3/1e6/1e9/1e12 across every archetype refuses NOT ONE case. WHAT SURVIVES, and what this entry now records: P4.9's criterion is scale-free only BELOW the declared reference magnitude of 10^3; above it the declared absolute ceiling of 1e-8 binds, and the worst faithfully restated period — lease_only_no_funded_debt.json period 0, restated x1000 — lands at residual 9.9035e-9 against that ceiling, a margin of 0.97%, reporting binding_term "declared_absolute_ceiling" and within_declared_envelope false. scripts/run_metamorphic_tests.mjs pins that margin as a measured number rather than as prose.
known_defects.consequence: No issuer is refused for its reporting unit today: a faithful restatement is accepted at every scale tested, x1e3 through x1e12. What remains is that ABOVE the declared reference magnitude the verdict is decided by a constant rather than by the magnitudes it judges, so a large-magnitude issuer is judged more leniently in relative terms than a small one, and the worst case in the corpus already sits within 1% of that constant. A modest deterioration anywhere in that neighbourhood becomes a refusal whose cause is a presentation choice. HIGH -> MEDIUM: the mechanism is real and structurally live; the registered consequence was not.
known_defects.repair_owner: PARTIALLY REPAIRED. P4.9 landed the scale-relative criterion in scripts/lib/solver.mjs (convergenceCriterion, 176-320) with the absolute ceiling DECLARED rather than silently applied. Removing the ceiling means raising the reference magnitude to policy.solver.relative_tolerance (D34) and is a joint change with three other readers plus a golden regeneration — specified, not attempted. The contaminating guard (D33) was repaired by P7.9 in scripts/lib/metamorphic_relations.mjs, which is where the false reproduction came from.
known_defects.retirement_condition: Retire when the declared absolute ceiling stops binding — that is, when every period of every faithfully restated archetype reports within_declared_envelope true, which requires the reference magnitude to rise to the declared relative tolerance (D34). Until then the check "MG-3's mechanism is REAL and MEDIUM" in scripts/run_metamorphic_tests.mjs pins the measured margin and fails if it either WIDENS (the mechanism was repaired without retiring this entry) or CLOSES (it became a refusal). Do NOT retire it because nothing is refused: nothing being refused is the corrected finding, not the repair.

known_defects.title: A row_type header row, which declares no values, is materialised into statement_values as numeric 0
known_defects.reproduction: Insert {row_id: 'hdr.income-statement', label: 'Year ended 31 December', row_type: 'header'} at the head of statement_structure.income_statement and the same shape at the tail, then solve. forecast[0].statement_values gains hdr.income-statement: 0 and hdr.cash-flow: 0 / hdr.cash-flow-repeat: 0. The rows carry no values key at all, so the zero is minted rather than read. Every solved economic quantity is byte-identical, which is why repeated_header stays declared economics-preserving with a PINNED delta.
known_defects.consequence: The repository's own doctrine is that an absent value never becomes a number (scripts/lib/case_generator.mjs PATHOLOGY_RAW / NON_NUMBER_PATHOLOGIES). A header row is the most common paginated-PDF artefact, so this is the path by which a layout artefact acquires a numeric identity in a value map. Also observed: the trailing header (hdr.income-statement-repeat) does NOT appear while the leading one does, so the two identical rows are not treated identically.
known_defects.repair_owner: scripts/lib/solver.mjs statement-value normalisation — FORBIDDEN to this package. Recorded, not repaired.
known_defects.retirement_condition: When header rows stop entering statement_values, the pinned delta becomes empty, this suite fails at the MG-4 reproduction assertion and this entry must be deleted.

known_defects.title: unit_scale_restatement assumes every operating metric is a magnitude, over a key space the schema leaves OPEN
known_defects.reproduction: `operating_metrics` is declared `additionalProperties: {$ref: metricSeries}` — an OPEN key space with six REQUIRED keys (revenue, adjusted_ebitda, depreciation_and_amortisation, change_in_working_capital, capex, tax). The transform scales `metric.values` for EVERY key with no dimension test of any kind. All eleven keys the corpus carries today are magnitudes, so nothing misfires; but a margin, a yield, a headcount, a store count or a per-unit price added under this open key space would be multiplied by the unit factor with no guard and no error. Add `operating_metrics.gross_margin = {values: [0.42, ...]}` to any archetype and the restatement returns 420 for a 42% margin.
known_defects.consequence: Latent. The same failure mode as D33 — a magnitude assumption applied to something that is not a magnitude — but reached by having NO test rather than a wrong one. It cannot be repaired the way D33 was: a total classification requires a closed key set, and this one is open by declaration. Either the schema closes `operating_metrics` (owned by the model-case schema, not by this layer) or each metric declares its own dimension.
known_defects.repair_owner: assets/model-case-v2.schema.json — FORBIDDEN to P7.9 (a schema change with compiler, solver and golden readers). Recorded, not repaired. The transform is left scaling every metric rather than being narrowed, because narrowing it silently would make the relation vacuous on any metric it stopped touching.
known_defects.retirement_condition: When operating_metrics declares a per-metric dimension, or the schema closes the key set and this register classifies it the way it classifies cash_policy.buckets[] — at which point the transform reads the declaration and this entry is deleted.

known_defects.title: A statement row's dimension is decided by a role the model-case schema leaves as an open string, and 13 of the 32 roles the corpus uses are untyped
known_defects.reproduction: unit_scale_restatement holds a row fixed when its semantic_role is a ratio and scales it otherwise. P7.9 replaced the hand-written one-element set with the set the statement taxonomy declares — roles carrying numeric_types ['percentage'], which is {margin, effective_tax_rate} — closing the `margin` gap. The RESIDUAL is that statementRow.semantic_role is declared {"type": "string"}, an open key space, and assets/statement-semantic-taxonomy.v1.json types only some of its roles: of the 32 distinct roles the corpus uses, 13 carry no numeric_types and 4 (cash_flow_da, discontinued_operation, rcf_draw, rcf_repayment) are absent from the taxonomy entirely. Every one of those is scaled by omission. All 32 happen to be magnitudes today, so nothing misfires; add a row with semantic_role 'gross_margin' and values [0.42, ...] and the restatement returns 420.
known_defects.consequence: Latent, and the same class as MG-6: a magnitude assumption reached by having no declaration to consult rather than by consulting the wrong one. It cannot be closed inside this layer — a total classification needs either a closed role enum or a numeric_types entry on every role, and both live in assets the metamorphic layer only reads.
known_defects.repair_owner: assets/statement-semantic-taxonomy.v1.json (give every declared role a numeric_types) and/or assets/model-case-v2.schema.json (close semantic_role to the taxonomy's ids) — both FORBIDDEN to P7.9 and both carrying compiler and classifier readers. Recorded, not repaired.
known_defects.retirement_condition: When every role the corpus uses carries a declared numeric_types, at which point unit_scale_restatement can throw on an untyped role the way it throws on an unclassified commitment-fee convention, and this entry is deleted.

unit_scale_class_reasons.net_leverage: a leverage multiple: a ratio of two currency quantities, so a unit restatement must leave it alone
unit_scale_class_reasons.rcf_average_fx: an FX rate, not a magnitude — a unit restatement of the reporting currency does not move a rate
unit_scale_class_reasons.rcf_ending_fx: an FX rate, not a magnitude
unit_scale_class_reasons.rcf_opening_fx: an FX rate, not a magnitude
unit_scale_class_reasons.instrument_results: an array of per-instrument records; the scaling relation is asserted over the scalar economic fields, and P4.6 declares the instrument family uncovered by the graph
unit_scale_class_reasons.statement_values: a per-row value map keyed by the case's own row ids, which vary case to case

unit_scale_class_semantics.currency: scales by exactly the declared scale_factor under unit_scale_restatement
unit_scale_class_semantics.invariant: unchanged under unit_scale_restatement — a ratio or a rate, never a magnitude
unit_scale_class_semantics.structured_not_scale_checked: a nested structure rather than a scalar; named here so its exclusion is declared, not silent

unit_restatement_dimensions.why: D33. `unit_scale_restatement` decided whether rcf_policy.commitment_fee_value was a magnitude or a rate by testing the SPELLING of commitment_fee_convention against /rate/i. No convention this repository admits contains the letters r-a-t-e, so the guard never fired and a 35bp fee was restated as 35,000bp — a 350% fee — whose non-convergence was then reported as a scale-invariance defect of the solver. A transform must take a quantity's dimension from a DECLARATION, never from a name. This register is that declaration, and it is checked TOTAL against the governing schema at import, so a newly admitted convention or key cannot fall into a class by default: it fails loudly until it is classified here.

dimension_semantics.monetary: a magnitude denominated in the issuer's reporting unit. SCALE-COVARIANT: a unit restatement multiplies it by the declared scale_factor.
dimension_semantics.rate: a rate, ratio, price-per-unit or multiple, denominated in its own dimensionless unit (basis points, a percentage, a fraction). SCALE-INVARIANT: a unit restatement must leave it exactly alone, because the unit it is expressed in is not the unit being restated.
dimension_semantics.declared_zero_placeholder: the schema requires the field but the governing convention forces it to an explicit zero and no reader consumes it as a magnitude. It has no dimension, so it is held fixed rather than scaled; scaling it would be a no-op today and a silent misclassification the day it stopped being zero.
dimension_semantics.non_numeric: free text or a structural value that carries no magnitude at all, so no scaling relation applies to it.

enum_authority.note: The governing schema for every case this transform sees. Every value it admits MUST be classified below.

additional_enum_authorities.note: The legacy model-case schema. It admits percent_of_margin, which model-case-v2 does not; classified here so a case arriving through the legacy path cannot be misclassified by omission.
The case-source schema the compiler reads. It admits bps_on_committed, which neither model-case schema does; classified here for the same reason.

none.reason: No fee is charged. coverage.mjs requires an explicit zero for this convention (scripts/lib/coverage.mjs:1605), and solver.mjs forces the applied rate to 0 (scripts/lib/solver.mjs:2737). The field carries no magnitude.

bps_on_undrawn.reason: Basis points applied to the average undrawn commitment: solver.mjs divides the value by 10000 and multiplies it by a currency balance (scripts/lib/solver.mjs:2737-2741). Basis points are dimensionless, so a restatement of the reporting unit must not move it. This is the value D33 scaled.

captured_in_residual.reason: The fee is already inside the reported unallocated-interest residual, so the field is stamped to an explicit 0 at ingress (scripts/lib/attachment_ingress.mjs:2192) and is admitted only for an explicitly unpriced facility (scripts/lib/coverage.mjs:1623). No reader consumes it as a magnitude.

percent_of_margin.reason: A percentage of the drawn margin: a fraction of a rate, therefore itself dimensionless. Admitted by the legacy model-case schema only; no case in the tree carries it, and it is classified here so that the day one does, it is not scaled.

bps_on_committed.reason: Basis points applied to the committed capacity rather than the undrawn portion. Same dimension as bps_on_undrawn; only the balance it is applied to differs. Admitted by the case-source schema only.

schema_authority.note: $defs/cashBucket declares additionalProperties:false, so this key set is exhaustive.

keyed_quantities.found_by: P7.9's sweep for D33's siblings. The retired guard was `key !== "eligible_percentage"`, a denylist of ONE key that is not a property of cashBucket at all — the real keys are net_debt_eligible_percentage, interest_eligible_percentage and cash_yield. The guard was therefore always true, and the transform multiplied two rates the schema bounds to [0,1] and a yield series by the unit factor, producing a case that violates its own schema. No case in the corpus carries buckets today, so it never fired in anger; it is dead code guarding a live branch, which is the same shape as D33.

bucket_id.reason: An identifier matching ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$. It carries no magnitude.

label.reason: The bucket's presentation caption. It carries no magnitude.

historical_year_end.reason: A three-series of cash balances at each historical year end, in the reporting unit. A magnitude, so it restates with the unit.

forecast_treatment.reason: The declared enum balancing / hardcode / flat / linked_debt_addback. It carries no magnitude.

included_in_cash_flow_cash.reason: A boolean saying whether the bucket forms part of the cash-flow statement's cash. It carries no magnitude.

linked_instrument_ids.reason: An array of instrument identifiers. It carries no magnitude.

forecast_values.reason: A three-series of forecast cash balances, or null. A magnitude, so it restates with the unit.

available_for_liquidity.reason: A boolean saying whether the bucket is usable liquidity. It carries no magnitude.

net_debt_eligible_percentage.reason: The fraction of the bucket that counts against net debt, bounded by the schema to [0, 1]. Dimensionless: scaling it by the unit factor produces a case that violates its own schema maximum. This is one of the three the retired guard scaled.

interest_eligible_percentage.reason: The fraction of the bucket that earns interest, bounded by the schema to [0, 1]. Dimensionless, for the same reason, and also scaled by the retired guard.

cash_yield.reason: A three-series of yields applied to the bucket balance. A rate series, not a magnitude, and also scaled by the retired guard.

source_line_ids.reason: An array of source-line identifiers. It carries no magnitude.

schema_authority.note: The schema declares additionalProperties:false, so this key set is exhaustive and the classification below can be TOTAL over it.

reported_opening_gross_debt.reason: Reported gross debt in the reporting currency, as a scalar or as a three-series. A magnitude, so it restates with the unit.

maximum_residual_percentage.reason: A tolerance expressed as a fraction of the reported balance (schema bounds it to [0, 0.05]). Dimensionless, so a unit restatement must not move it.

note.reason: Free text recording how the reconciliation was struck. It carries no magnitude.
